validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED, independent of GEM. The sheet's own citation pool for this row (9 harvested citations from the FGT gem.wiki page) is thin for this specific sub-project: citation [1] is a bit.ly link that resolves to abarrelfull.wikidot.com (BANNED — skipped per standing rule 5, and per url_verifier's SHORTENER_HOSTS note bit.ly links on this batch are known to hide abarrelfull); citation [4] (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php) is the navigation page, not a document, per this batch's measured conditions. Neither, as harvested, actually supports the row. So I went past the navigation page to the actual downloadable dataset it links to: EIA's 'U.S. Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (Jan2021 edition), sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2020)', row 323/1038. It names the project 'FGT AE Cooperative Upgrade' (exact name match), operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', status 'Completed', in-service/completed date 2001-11-08 (Year In Service: 2001 — matches GEM's StartYear1 exactly, and gives StartMonth1 = November, currently blank on the sheet), states 'MS,AL' (Beg_State MS / End_State AL — both currently blank on the sheet, only 'United States'/'United States' filled), cost $6.9 million (GEM's SegmentCost is $7,000,000 — a ~1.4% rounding-level variance, not material), Additional Capacity 80 MMcf/d (GEM's Capacity: exact match), Pipeline Diameter '30,36' in (GEM's Diameter: exact match), Pipeline Type 'Interstate', Authority 'FERC', Docket Number 'CP00-40'. Project type 'Expansion' — correctly classified as a gas transmission expansion on FGT's interstate mainline, not a gathering/process line; Fuel=Gas is correct (the workbook itself is EIA's natural-gas pipeline projects table). Checked the roster for a duplicate: none of the other 16 FGT project-name rows in this batch (Phase IV/V/VI/VII/VIII, East Leg, Western Division, Jacksonville, Sanford, Turkey Point, Alabama Power, Mobile Bay, East Louisiana, South Alabama) share this project's name, docket, or figures — 'AE Cooperative Upgrade' is a distinct FERC certificate facility (likely serving Alabama Electric Cooperative / PowerSouth Energy Cooperative, a rural electric co-op with gas-fired generation in south Alabama), not a relabel of a sibling row. Docket CP00-40 is shared with three OTHER named EIA rows (FGT Phase V Stages 1-2, Stage 3, and Stage 4) — i.e. one FERC certificate proceeding authorized several related facilities including this one; that is a normal FERC pattern (a single docket can cover several discrete authorized facilities/stages) and not evidence of a duplicate. TIER: medium, not high — I could not reach a second, fully independent source: elibrary.ferc.gov (for docket CP00-40 itself) is an Angular SPA behind Cloudflare that returns only a JS shell to a scripted client (no accessible API endpoint found — tried /eLibrary/api/docket/, /api/dockets/, /api/docket-sheet, /eLibrary/docket-sheet, all either JS-shell 200s or Cloudflare-challenged); this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I could search for the docket or 'AE Cooperative' independently, and DuckDuckGo (html + lite) and a scripted fetch of Bing both returned bot-challenge pages with no usable results. Of the row's other harvested citations: kindermorgan.com's FGT page (cite [5]) now 404s (KM sold out of FGT in 2021, irrelevant to existence, not a deletion of a GEM ref since it was never cited on THIS unit); fgttransfer.energytransfer.com's system-map portal (cite [2]) returned 200 but is a login/JS shell with no extractable content; eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php (cite [3]) is a generic map-legend page, no project content; fractracker.org's national map article (cite [7]) returned 200 but never names FGT or this project; oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 (cite [9]) is a Vue SPA that serves only a JS shell to curl (no API endpoint discovered); the Pipeline News PDF (cite [10], 2018) and texasenergyreport.com article (cite [11], 2018, paywalled/empty to a scripted fetch) both concern a different, much later FGT expansion (East-West/2018-19), not this 2001 project. 8 of 9 harvested citations opened; 1 (oilandgaswatch SPA) could not be rendered without a JS-executing client. Recommend a human with browser/FERC-eLibrary access pull docket CP00-40 directly for a true second, fully independent confirmation and precise Proposal/Construction dates.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown = 0.00 mi conflicts with EIA's Historical Projects table, which states 0.2 miles for 'FGT AE Cooperative Upgrade' (same row that exact-matches on name, capacity, diameter, docket and year). LengthKnown=0 is the correct convention only for an expansion with NO new physical pipe (compression/metering only) — but this row's Diameter is filled with real values (30, 36 in), which is inconsistent with a no-new-pipe upgrade and IS consistent with EIA's 0.2 mi (a short tie-in/lateral segment, ~1,000 ft). I did not stage a fills[] object confirming the existing 0.00 value with this ref, since that would silently paper over a real disagreement; flagging here instead so Update can apply the corrected value (0.2 mi) together with this same ref.

validity.recommendation: verify Owner1 — Energy Transfer's own site states FGT is owned through 'Citrus,' a 50/50 Kinder Morgan / Energy Transfer joint venture, not solely by 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100%; check whether this applies across all 17 FGT rows in this batch
validity.researcher_notes: The Owner [ref] cell carries 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100%, unreferenced. Energy Transfer's own operations page (energytransfer.com/operations/) states in its FGT entry: 'FGT is owned by Citrus, a 50/50 joint venture with Kinder Morgan, Inc. ("KMI")' — i.e. per the direct operator/co-owner's own disclosure, the pipeline's equity ownership sits one level up, split 50/50 between KMI and Energy Transfer via the Citrus Corp joint venture, not concentrated 100% in the LLC that holds the FERC certificate. This mirrors the gem.wiki page's own infobox, which lists 'Parent company: Kinder Morgan [50%]; Energy Transfer Partners [50%]' for this same segment — i.e. GEM's own wiki page disagrees with GEM's own sheet value on this row. I can't rule out that GEM's Owner1/Owner2... columns are deliberately tracking the asset-owning LLC rather than the equity structure (a legitimate schema choice), so I'm flagging rather than asserting a fix — but given this looks like a systemic pattern (likely identical Owner1=100% FGT Co LLC on some or all of the other 16 FGT rows in this batch, all one operating company), it's worth a single decision applied across the whole FGT cluster rather than row-by-row guessing.
